reason: The Stripe secret key is hardcoded in the client-side environment configuration (environment.ts line 5) and used directly in an HTTP Authorization header from the browser (payment.service.ts line 12). This exposes the secret to anyone who can view the compiled JavaScript or intercept network requests, allowing unauthorized use of the Stripe account.

The frontend code exposes a Stripe live secret key (sk_live_...) in environment.ts and transmits it via Authorization header to the application's own backend API. Secret keys must never be present in frontend code or sent over the network from the client; they should only be used server-side. This allows anyone with access to the frontend bundle to extract the secret key and make arbitrary Stripe API calls.

The access token is stored in localStorage, which is accessible to any JavaScript running on the page. This makes it vulnerable to theft via XSS attacks. No mitigating control (such as httpOnly cookies, token encryption, or short-lived tokens with refresh rotation) is present in the code shown.
